# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report security problems **privately** by email to
[opensource@grow.codes](mailto:opensource@grow.codes). Do not open a public issue, pull request or
discussion for a suspected vulnerability.

Include as much of the following as you can:

- the affected package(s) and version(s) (`@grow-codes/zipkin`, `grow-zipkin` crate,
  `github.com/grow-codes-packages/zipkin/go`, `grow-zipkin` on PyPI, `codes.grow.packages:zipkin`),
- a description of the problem and its impact,
- steps to reproduce or a proof of concept,
- whether the problem is already public.

Never send real credentials, tokens or production data. Use throwaway values.

## What to expect

| Step | Target |
| - | - |
| Acknowledgement of your report | 3 working days |
| First assessment (accepted / declined, severity) | 10 working days |
| Fix released for critical and high severity issues | as fast as possible, normally within 30 days |

We will keep you informed, agree a disclosure date with you, and credit you in the release notes and
the GitHub security advisory unless you prefer to stay anonymous.

## Supported versions

Only the latest minor release of each package receives security fixes. All five language packages
are released from this repository with the same feature set; a fix is shipped in every affected
language.

| Version | Supported |
| - | - |
| latest minor (`x.y`) | yes |
| older releases | no — please upgrade |

## Scope

In scope: the code in this repository (all language packages, the Docker test harness and the
release workflows).

Out of scope: vulnerabilities in Zipkin itself — please report those to The OpenZipkin authors — and in
third-party dependencies unless this project uses them in an unsafe way.

## How the packages protect secrets

- Credentials are held in redacting secret types; `toString`/debug/JSON output shows `[REDACTED]`.
- Error messages, hook data and log output pass through redaction of known secret values, sensitive
  headers, query parameters and fields.
- Proxy environment variables are ignored unless a proxy is configured explicitly.
- TLS verification is on by default; `insecureSkipVerify` is meant for tests and logs a warning.

If you find a way to make any of these leak a secret, that is a vulnerability — please report it.
